claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a dense, monolithic microstructure.
HfMoTaTiZr powder can be processed by laser powder bed fusion into a complex 3D lattice.
The proposed lattice will have sub-millimeter struts and optimized node geometries.
The engineered lattice architecture introduces controlled internal voids.
The lattice struts and nodes distribute applied stresses efficiently.
Introducing controlled voids reduces material volume and therefore lowers component-level effective density.
Optimized lattice geometry concentrates load in robust struts that remain mechanically effective at high temperatures.
The optimized geometry prevents the strength loss that would otherwise accompany reducing the amount of alloy in the component.
The lattice-architected component will have lower effective density than monolithic as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The lattice-architected component will retain yield strength comparable to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr at room temperature.
The lattice-architected component will retain yield strength comparable to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr at approximately 1000 °C.
The lattice-architected component will retain creep resistance comparable to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr at approximately 1000 °C.
The hypothesis is intended to apply from room temperature through approximately 1000 °C under static and dynamic structural loads.
The balance between density reduction and strength retention depends on lattice-design parameters and LPBF processing consistency.
